summary: Monolithic system-prompt causes deadline_exceeded 504s when batched priming requests hit finalizer queue
description: Customer reports deterministic 504 deadline_exceeded errors when sending batched generation requests that include a single very large system prompt (massive priming document ~65k tokens). Failures appear only when batching is enabled and multiple customer requests target the same serving shard concurrently. The requests succeed when sent individually or when the system prompt is trimmed below ~8k tokens.
impact: Several production endpoints for StellarDocs' document-summarization product are returning 504s for long-document priming workflows. Approx 12% of requests in a customer job queue are failing, causing downstream ingestion retries and billing discrepancies. Customer is on Dedicated capacity; priority to avoid SLA breach for this tenant.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Tenant uses model redwood-instruct-30b (dedicated pool)
2) Compose request with a single system prompt containing a concatenated doc ~65k tokens and user prompt for summarization, request max_tokens=4096
3) Submit 8 parallel requests with batching_enabled=true and batch_affinity=on
4) Observe final response: 504 with body indicating deadline_exceeded and 'finalizer exceeded deadline' in logs.
5) Repeat with batching_enabled=false or trim system prompt to <8k tokens: requests succeed.
logs:
Snippet from serving logs:
[2026-03-10T14:12:02.843Z] shard-07 finalizer: deadline_exceeded after 90s while waiting for kv-append lock
[2026-03-10T14:12:02.844Z] kernel-swap: initiated due to memory pressure; evicted 3 KV slabs
[2026-03-10T14:12:02.845Z] http-gateway: request_id=abc123 status=504 reason=deadline_exceeded
Customer-side client logs show connection closed by server after 90s. Grafana traces: spike in finalizer queue length and prefetch latency correlated to these events (link in investigation_notes).
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: Large single system prompt causes excessive KV append/serialization time during prefix caching, amplified when multiple requests are batched and affinity pins them to same GPU. Observed pattern: interleaved KV writes cause slab thrash and kernel swap, finalizer waits exceed per-request finalizer timeout (90s). Reproduced in staging by replaying customer's payloads.
Metrics: finalizer_queue_length spiked to 120 (baseline 5) on shard-07 at failure window. Kernel swap frequency increased by 3x.
Triage actions: reproduced with a synthetic payload derived from customer's prompt. Disabled batch_affinity for the tenant; request success rate returned to ~98%. Collected pprof of finalizer during reproduction; attached to PR.
Potential root causes: (a) tactical finalizer timeout too short for cross-request KV thrash, (b) aggressive batching policies that don't account for oversized prompt tokenization cost, (c) lack of preflight tokenization guard in API layer.

Support (Anita Shah) 2026-03-10: Logged ticket after customer supplied failing request corpus and trace IDs.
SRE (Marco Rivera) 2026-03-10: Reproduced in staging, disabled batch_affinity for tenant as temporary mitigation.
Customer (StellarOps) 2026-03-11: Confirmed reduction in 504s after mitigation but asked for permanent fix and guidance for best practices.
Eng (Evelyn Brooks) 2026-03-11: Requested pprof and heap snapshots; created linked PR to increase finalizer timeout and add preflight tokenization warning.
Support (Anita Shah) 2026-03-12: Sent workaround guidance to customer and scheduled follow-up call to discuss optimal priming strategies.
resolution:
Temporary mitigation: disabled batch_affinity for the tenant and increased per-request finalizer timeout for their dedicated pool from 90s -> 180s. Customer notices immediate drop in 504s. Permanent fix (in progress): PR #984 to add API preflight that tokenizes large system prompts and returns a clear 4xx with guidance when prompts exceed safe thresholds; PR #986 to make batching policy avoid co-locating oversized priming requests on same shard. Postmortem action: add a telemetry-derived warning in Console when >75% of a request's token budget is occupied by system prompt.
Related PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/984, github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/986
Confluence runbook: https://confluence.redwood.internal/runbooks/large-prompt-timeouts
